# `conductor`

Generated by `conductor-docs` from the clap definition of the `conductor` command line in [`crates/conductor/src/cli.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/conductor/blob/main/crates/conductor/src/cli.rs). It lists only commands that exist; `--help` after any command prints the same text.

> The records conductor and the repository controllers keep

## Global options

Every command takes these, before or after its name.

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--state-dir <DIR>` | no | none | The state directory; conductor's records are kept in its tree/. Default: the instance's state when a config file names it, else state/ under the working directory |
| `--config <FILE>` | no | none | The config file, named by `globals.config` of the binding. Default: $CONDUCTOR_CONFIG, else ~/.b10x/conductor/conductor.yaml. Every command reads it for its instance |

## `conductor watch run`

Watch sessions, usage limits, conductor's context, free disk and main's CI; exit after the first pass that finds a change

```text
Usage: conductor watch run [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--every <SECONDS>` | no | none | Seconds from the end of one pass over the sessions, usage limits, conductor's context and free disk to the start of the next. Default: 180 |
| `--ci-every <SECONDS>` | no | none | Seconds between two reads of main's CI; the first pass always reads it. Default: 900 |
| `--follow <BOOL>` | no | none | Print each change and go on watching, rather than exit after the first pass that finds one. `--follow` alone is `--follow true` One of `true`, `false`. |
